rule: Elixir: ... A `use`d module's injected imports and aliases resolve through its source (the scan, dependency sources, the standard library); with one import known to export the name, that import is the target.
source: KNOWN_GAP: calls generated by macros whose source is not read (a use of a library outside the scan) stay low bare names; pass dependency sources as reference_paths
notes: call_type convention (SPEC gives no Elixir mapping; Elixir has no methods and the `macro` type is defined only for C/C++/ObjC and Rust `name!`): every local, imported and remote call is direct, a call through a value is callback. Operators and special forms (`|>`, `=`, `case`, `fn`, `%{}`, `__MODULE__`) are language constructs, not calls. Bare Kernel functions resolve to the auto-imported Kernel (Elixir decision: 'with one import known to export the name, that import is the target'): `Kernel.<name>`, medium. ExUnit.Case is outside the scan but in the standard library (ExUnit ships with Elixir). Its `__using__` injects `import ExUnit.Callbacks`, `import ExUnit.Assertions`, `import ExUnit.Case, only: [describe: 2, test: 1, test: 2, test: 3]` and `import ExUnit.DocTest`; of these only ExUnit.Assertions exports `flunk` (a function, `def flunk(message \\ "Flunked!")`). So `flunk` is `ExUnit.Assertions.flunk`, medium (named statically, not defined in the scan), not a low bare `flunk`. Calls that ExUnit's quote injects into the module are not written in src/ and are not expected.
